title: Reduction of a flat module modulo an ideal is flat over the quotient ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq R$ an ideal and $M$ a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $M/JM$, an $R/J$-module by $(r\bmod J)\cdot(x\bmod JM)=rx\bmod JM$, is a flat $R/J$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change, line 8888) applied to $R\to R'=R/J$, together with the canonical isomorphism $M\otimes_RR/J\cong M/JM$ (right exactness of $M\otimes_R-$ applied to $J\to R\to R/J\to0$); used in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0C4G ('Hence $B^\wedge/\mathfrak m_A^nB^\wedge$ is flat over $A/\mathfrak m_A^n$')
